security_audit.summary: The 32 static external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline backticks in SKILL.md. The skill contains guidance only and declares Read, Glob, and Grep as allowed tools. I found one semantic concern: the security audit pattern references active vulnerability testing without explicit authorization boundaries.

remediation.issue: Security testing pattern lacks explicit authorization boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance that penetration testing and exploit checks must target only owned or authorized systems, with scope confirmed before active tests.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Authorization Guardrails For Active Testing
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md describes a security audit chain that sends work to a penetration-tester for active vulnerability testing and lists red team and exploit as triggers. It does not state that testing must be authorized or scoped.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly mention active vulnerability testing and exploit-related trigger phrases. The concern is scoped because the skill itself is documentation and declares read-only tools.

content.value_statement: Complex work often needs several expert reviews at once. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured way to assign agents, pass context, and synthesize results.
actual_capabilities: Shows prompts for invoking single agents, sequential chains, and resumed agent work.
Defines orchestration patterns for comprehensive analysis, feature review, and security audit workflows.
Lists 17 specialized agent roles with matching trigger phrases.
Describes how built-in Explore, Plan, and general-purpose agents fit the workflow.
Provides a synthesis report format for combining agent findings and action items.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or automation code.
Depends on agents that may not exist in every Claude Code or Codex setup.
Does not enforce authorization checks for security testing requests.
Requires the main assistant to manage task scope and final synthesis.

use_cases.title: Run Multi-Perspective Code Reviews
use_cases.description: Coordinate security, backend, frontend, and testing agents before a major merge.

use_cases.title: Plan Cross-Stack Features
use_cases.description: Route feature work through domain agents and collect one implementation plan.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Release Checks
use_cases.description: Use specialist agents to review security, tests, documentation, and performance before release.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to coordinate agents for a small code review. Ask one explorer agent to map the files, then one test engineer to list test gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend, frontend, and test agents to review the checkout feature. Pass findings between agents and give one final recommendation list.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate security, performance, and documentation agents for a release candidate. Separate blocking issues from follow-up improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate Full Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multi-agent workflow for a database-backed feature. Include discovery, implementation review, tests, documentation, and a final synthesis.

output_examples.output: The skill would assign explorer, security, backend, and testing agents. The final output would combine risks, missing tests, and prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: Plan a feature that touches API, UI, and database schema.
output_examples.output: The skill would route work to backend, frontend, database, and testing agents. It would return a unified action plan with ownership areas.

output_examples.input: Synthesize results from several agent reviews.
output_examples.output: The output would group agent contributions, shared recommendations, and final action items in one readable report.

best_practices: Start with an explorer or planning agent when the affected files are unclear.
Pass concise findings from earlier agents to later agents.
End with one synthesis that ranks issues by user impact and security risk.
anti_patterns: Do not use orchestration for simple edits that one agent can handle.
Do not run security testing on systems without clear authorization.
Do not paste separate agent reports without resolving conflicts.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate multiple specialized AI agents and combine their findings into one final response.

faq.question: Does it run external scripts?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-only and limits allowed tools to Read, Glob, and Grep.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace lists Codex support, but actual subagent availability depends on your environment.

faq.question: Is every listed agent always available?
faq.answer: No. The listed agents are role patterns. Your environment must provide matching agents.

faq.question: How should I use it for security work?
faq.answer: Use it only for authorized assets. Keep scope, targets, and testing limits explicit.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a consolidated synthesis with agent contributions, recommendations, and action items.
